51296: Soto has three substantial MLB seasons, including 708 PA, 35 HR and 121 unintentional walks at origin, but no own minor contact in the window. The primary and all-player forecasts therefore stay exactly +3.941 and 634 expected PA. Refitted raw heads are saved but deliberately not applied. His +5.516 observed rate and 713 PA remain a miss of the existing system, not evidence about Soto's contact cells. Profar, Castro, Gurriel and Arozarena are same-position workload controls with different talent; their substantial following-year PA cannot explain away a superstar batting miss.
44122: Julio had 340 current A+/AA PA, 13 HR and 42 walks; 2020 is canceled evidence, not poor production. Coverage raises hitting from +1.216 to +1.317, while adding contact mix drops it to +1.101 and joint detail recovers only +1.109, below his +2.683 actual rate. In the joint fitted sum, mix contributes -0.358 and detail -0.048, while coverage contributes +0.310. Those are within-fit terms, not the total refit difference. The unchanged 254 expected PA also misses 560. Refined active support is thirteen people. Position-selected peers have much lower ranks, including Valera at .54 versus Julio .98; their non-arrivals are not equivalent superstar readiness evidence. This is a retained harm, not a reason to ban all contact shapes.
33263: Alonso supplied 574 current AA/AAA PA with 36 HR and 73 walks. The three contact variants improve his forecast modestly, but most of the gain already occurs with coverage alone: +0.592 becomes +0.721 before +0.733 with shape and +0.726 with joint detail. The joint detail block contributes +0.121 inside its refitted sum, yet its forecast is slightly below the shape-only fit. Do not describe a fitted block contribution as the between-model gain. Both +0.726 versus +3.283 actual hitting and 215 versus 693 PA remain serious underestimates. Only one person matches the refined active profile. The original school class is unknown, not evidence he did not attend college; earlier cached school recovery was separately tested and is not silently imported here. Rooker and Thaiss are useful broad draft/exposure comparisons, not identical talent or timing.
33359: Collins had 531 AA PA, 15 HR, 99 walks and 158 strikeouts. Coverage's delivered value is near actual, but that is an ordinary value case rather than an accurate batting or workload forecast: expected PA is 28 versus 102, and even its -0.011 hitting estimate exceeds the -1.932 observed rate. Joint detail raises the rate to +0.325, making the hitting error worse; its detail block adds +0.218. Center-field fly outs contribute +0.146 in this saved linear sum. That association may proxy other correlated production/context and is not proof that an out is inherently valuable. Pentecost and Okey do not arrive, while Rogers and Smith do. Preserve the compensating component errors rather than declaring this a solved ordinary player.
57052: Kurtz has only 50 professional PA, four HR and 27 classified contacts, with correct fourth-pick and college-junior evidence already present. Joint detail barely changes translated hitting, +1.024 to +1.031; its within-fit detail block is negative despite a positive pulled-fly HR term. Zero active training people match even the coarse thin-contact upper-minors profile. His 6.06% arrival chance and ten expected PA versus 489 actual remain the dominant delivered-value miss. His extraordinary +5.150 first-year hitting is also not captured. The first-base restriction leaves older and lower-ranked college peers, not equivalent newly drafted top-four prospects; Kayfus appears and Morales/Lorusso/Boeve do not. These peers do not justify the low Kurtz arrival forecast or certify a precise tiny-sample talent grade.
34859: Reynolds had 383 AA PA with seven HR, forty walks and 73 strikeouts after 541 A+ PA. Repaired contacts are present in three seasons and the current 264 physical contacts include the restored identity. Hitting improves slightly from -0.639 to -0.544, but joint detail itself contributes just +0.005; exposure and reestimated old terms matter more. Both estimates remain far below +2.731 actual MLB hitting. Fixed 15.64% times 81 conditional PA still gives only thirteen expected PA versus 546. Broad/refined active support is 134/68, so this is not explained simply by no general training examples. Bishop, Calica, Lipka and Tom are draft/exposure neighbors, not demonstrated equal talent. The contact repair and raw block do not resolve this substantial readiness and hitting miss.
33832: Jackson's current 377 AA/AAA PA include 120 strikeouts and eight HR. Joint detail raises hitting from -0.736 to -0.425, making the error worse against an exceptionally poor fifteen-PA MLB sample. It is the largest unweighted active-rate harm, not the largest PA-weighted harm: the latter receives a separate Torkelson walkthrough. The predicted direction recognizes some power/contact evidence but still underweights his high strikeout risk in this fitted comparison. The within-fit detail block adds +0.062, led by a positive center-fly-out term. Those correlations are not causal baseball values. Forty expected PA versus fifteen is a smaller absolute workload miss. Three origin-selected catchers do not arrive and Smith does; tiny actual batting samples remain highly uncertain rather than a target for fitting a fifteen-PA collapse.
33567: McNeil had 384 minor PA with nineteen HR and low strikeouts, followed by 248 MLB PA with only 24 strikeouts. Primary forecasts deliberately remain -0.243 because he had debuted. The all-player sensitivity uses recent measured minor contact and raises hitting to +0.188, moving toward +3.357 actual. Coverage and mix refits also contribute; the joint within-fit detail term is +0.127, not the full +0.431 change. Expected PA remains 441 versus 567. Fletcher is a younger successful control; Torreyes and Gosselin receive small samples and d'Arnaud none. Their different histories do not establish equivalent talent. The sensitivity helps this actual young-MLB miss, but this case alone does not justify adopting the all-player route.
53595: Holliday's 581 current PA, twelve HR and 99 walks span A through AAA. Joint detail raises translated hitting from +0.826 to +0.924, worsening the false high against -2.838 actual. Coverage alone is more optimistic at +0.982; mix partly offsets that and detail adds +0.084 in the joint fitted sum. A strong nineteen-year-old prospect being projected above average is not physically impossible, but the actual first-year transition was much harder. Fixed 351 expected PA versus 208 compounds the miss. Refined active support is 22 people, not enough to erase transition uncertainty. Mayer, Montgomery and Williams do not arrive while Merrill plays 593 PA. Keep these outcomes and pedigree differences visible instead of assuming every top teenage prospect immediately produces.
54849: Judge supplied 696, 458 and 704 MLB PA with 62, 37 and 58 HR, but no own minor contacts in the window. Both assemblies retain +4.534 hitting and 531 expected PA exactly; the raw contact refits are not applied. His +6.287 observed rate and 679 PA remain existing-system errors. No measured Judge fly-ball attribution is available here, so the test cannot validate a full MLB contact model. Buxton, Mullins, Thomas and Varsho are position-selected workload controls with clearly different hitting ability, not equivalent star comparisons. The absence of contact evidence is explicit rather than converted into zero talent.
53164: Langford had 200 professional PA and ten HR, including eighty AA/AAA PA, plus fourth-pick/college-junior evidence. Joint detail raises hitting from +1.439 to +1.650, farther above his +0.549 actual first-year rate. The within-fit detail block contributes only +0.044; coverage and other refitted terms account for much of the move. Delivered value nevertheless gets slightly closer because the fixed 215 expected PA is much lower than 557 actual: optimistic talent partly masks underestimated workload. Refined active support is zero. Same-position college peers are older or later picks and do not arrive; they are not adequate elite-entry comparables. This is a concrete reason to score both components and delivered value rather than calling a value improvement a hitting improvement.
33319: Meadows supplied 285 current AAA PA with twelve HR and 191 MLB PA with six HR, alongside older minor production. Primary hitting remains -0.138 because he had debuted. The all-player sensitivity raises it to +0.195 and value .707 to .845, toward +3.009 hitting and 5.358 value observed, but still misses substantially. The joint detail block adds +0.058 within its fit; coverage alone and refitted original coefficients also change the estimate. Fixed PA stays 248 versus 591. Frazier, Williams, Quinn and Stevenson receive smaller following-year workloads. The repaired historical contact block gives this young incumbent a useful modest lift, not the large old detailed-model gain under a different target/population.
31364: Maitan's known batting source has 176 rookie PA, 49 strikeouts, ten walks and two HR. The repaired contact source retains distinct rookie league IDs, including 105 classified contacts across RK120/RK124; the legacy batting-count buckets do not align perfectly with that league granularity. Joint detail lowers hitting from -0.380 to -0.547, with -0.109 from detail inside the fitted sum. This is coherent caution about weak production, but no observed MLB hitting rate exists because he did not arrive. Two expected PA versus zero tests immediate contribution, not eventual career talent. Refined active support is zero. All four age/position peers also do not arrive; their unlisted pedigree differs. Do not convert non-arrival into a validated negative long-term batting grade.
42694: Azocar is an ordinary delivered-value case but not a solved opportunity forecast. His current 544 AA/AAA PA include nine HR; the AAA stint has no HR and six walks in 201 PA. Joint hitting -1.319 is close to -1.499 observed, with a negative -0.099 detail term, but only twelve expected MLB PA precede 216 actual. Value happens to be close because his realized offense plus replacement is near zero. Three selected peers do not arrive and Blanco gets seven PA, which illustrates uncertainty rather than explaining Azocar's much larger workload. Broad/refined active support is 297/117. Preserve this component mismatch instead of presenting a tiny value error as accurate player opportunity.
47909: Schneider had 454 current A+/AA/AAA PA with sixteen HR, 65 walks and 116 strikeouts. Joint contact improves the hitting forecast from -0.598 to -0.106, but remains far below his exceptional +5.351 over 141 MLB PA. Coverage alone already raises it to -0.387; shape adds another lift, and the joint detail block contributes +0.107 within the fitted sum. Pulled line-drive singles and center-field fly outs are positive terms in this fit. These are unadjusted associations, not universal values for outs. Twenty-three expected PA also misses 141. All four late-pick origin peers do not appear, with different upper-level exposure; the breakout is not predictable simply from their non-arrivals. This is the largest unweighted active-rate gain, not a repaired overall forecast.
48512: Carroll had 434 current AA/AAA PA with 23 HR, eight rookie PA and 115 MLB PA with four HR. The declared all-player route raises hitting from +0.869 to +1.587, toward +2.478 observed; it is the largest established-player value gain. Primary prospect-only forecasts remain unchanged. The joint fitted detail block contributes +0.137, while coverage contributes +0.189 and mix -0.043; the full +0.718 refit difference cannot be attributed to detail alone. PA stays 462 versus 645. Only four refined active people support this profile. Position-matched older peers are not equivalent elite twenty-one-year-olds. A useful young-MLB sensitivity does not settle full-cohort adoption, especially with public value worsening.
51950: Torkelson's 2023 MLB line has 684 PA and 31 HR after a poor first MLB year. No current MLB contact is measured; the new block uses recency-weighted 2021–22 minor contact. The all-player route raises hitting from +1.296 to +1.681, worsening the error against -0.721 actual, and raises already-high value from 2.872 to 3.223 versus .422 actual. Primary remains unchanged. His +0.127 within-fit detail term does not establish that old minor evidence should outweigh current MLB production. PA is fixed at 547 versus 381. Goldschmidt is much older and the other position peers have much smaller MLB histories. Keep this major sensitivity harm alongside Carroll's gain; no post-result route selects only favorable young incumbents.
35088: Alvarez had 379 current AA/AAA PA with twenty HR and forty walks after lower-level production. Joint hitting rises from +0.455 to +0.769, moving toward +5.648 actual and providing the largest actual-PA-weighted rate gain. Coverage contributes +0.212 inside its joint fit, mix +0.111 and detail only +0.041; most of the total improvement is not an isolated detailed-cell effect. The fixed 43.4% arrival chance times 166 conditional PA yields 72 expected versus 369 actual. Refined active support is four people. Arozarena has a small debut and the other position/exposure peers do not appear; their weaker pedigree/ranking and different production cannot explain away Alvarez's breakout. This useful direction remains a very large talent and readiness miss.
44348: Torkelson had 530 A+/AA/AAA PA, thirty HR and 76 walks at origin. Joint hitting rises from +0.878 to +1.304, farther from -1.766 actual, and is the largest actual-PA-weighted prospect-rate harm. Coverage alone supplies much of the rise; its joint within-fit term is +0.397, versus +0.038 mix and +0.035 detail. Fixed 155 expected PA is below 404, while optimistic talent drives positive value against a slightly negative outcome. Refined support is thirteen people. Donovan gets 468 PA and three position-selected peers none, but their lower draft/rank evidence differs from Torkelson's. Strong minor production legitimately supported optimism; the adverse MLB transition must nevertheless count, without fitting a manual rule to his name.
review_limits: All nineteen case identities and outcomes remain fixed. Position-first peer restrictions sometimes remove the best pedigree/readiness matches; peers are controls, not proof of equivalent talent. Historical school-class unknowns and actual-league/count-bucket differences are preserved. This comparison uses raw minor contact without park/opponent neutralization or current MLB contact, fixed opportunity and a linear learner. Neither uncertainty nor source correctness licenses a blanket conclusion about all detailed-contact modeling.
